title: Verified hardware improvements: evidence, throughput, and usability
description:
PLAN STATUS: backlog created; product implementation has not started.

CURRENT BASELINE
The inspected working tree has bounded Python/MATLAB-to-VHDL translation, exact-cycle RTL checking, independent development/audit data, Xilinx mapping and mapped replay, SHA chaining, SLAM cosimulation and legacy Wi-Fi. No AGENTS.md or pre-existing issue backlog was found; existing uncommitted work is the baseline.

SELECTION
Thirty candidates were evaluated against robustness, reliability, performance, intuitiveness, user-friendliness, ergonomics, usefulness, compellingness, accretiveness and pragmatism. Usefulness and pragmatism have weight 2, accretiveness 1.5; others weight 1. Scores are subjective judgments, not performance evidence. Any criterion=1 or average<3 is a hard cut. Final ordering also considers enabling value and bounded implementation scope.

1. Bind every verification claim to an immutable artifact bundle (fpga-2hx.1, P1, weighted score 4.84/5).
The project sells evidence of correctness. A user must be able to tell which exact source, netlist, tests and target justify a claim, even after moving final/ or rebuilding an image. Today partial provenance and independently edited reports make that answer harder than necessary. A checked bundle makes sharing a result, starting SLAM, and composing receiver blocks dependable, while a generated summary prevents stale documentation from understating or overstating success. This ranks first because it protects every downstream improvement, including caching and benchmarking, without changing arithmetic or the public hardware interface.

2. Make generation and audit recovery durable and deterministic (fpga-2hx.2, P1, weighted score 4.84/5).
A failed container or interrupted laptop session should cost unfinished work, not an entire experiment. Resume must also preserve what was actually tested: changing from RTL-only to mapping or replaying a different proposal cannot inherit an old success. Persisting the selected candidate before opening audit data makes the research boundary inspectable. The benefit is particularly concrete for the Wi-Fi flow, where builds take many minutes and each stage currently has its own recovery behavior.

3. Reuse verified compilation products while rerunning independent checks (fpga-2hx.3, P1, weighted score 4.60/5).
Compilation and mapping are deterministic work for a fixed artifact and toolchain; development and audit need different stimuli and scoring, not necessarily a second synthesis. Separating these stages can save substantial repeated work without weakening independence. The code has useful existing seams, especially the Wi-Fi mapped executable and SLAM server, so this is an incremental improvement. Speedup must be measured from stage timings; the plan makes no numerical performance promise in advance.

4. Unify FPGA resource accounting and explicit target budgets (fpga-2hx.4, P1, weighted score 4.68/5).
The same netlist should not receive different cost estimates depending on the command that produced it. Missing RAM LUTs can make a budget pass misleading, and fourteen 36-Kibit blocks should not be compared blindly with a budget expressed in 18-Kibit equivalents. Reusing the stronger existing Wi-Fi accounting makes resource gates easier to trust and produces a common baseline for compact-receiver work. This is bounded, testable work with immediate relevance to the repository.

5. Validate and explain hardware contracts before expensive generation (fpga-2hx.5, P1, weighted score 4.68/5).
An invalid vector, misunderstood bit layout or wrong file path should be found before a model call and several minutes of tool work. Structured input descriptions also reduce ambiguity when translating a new kernel. The existing strict dataclasses provide a good foundation; this idea adds an explanatory front end and optional metadata rather than relaxing validation. Audit isolation is central: normal generation preflight must not inspect or reveal audit values to the provider.

6. Schedule tool jobs within an explicit CPU and memory budget (fpga-2hx.6, P1, weighted score 4.52/5).
Per-container limits do not prevent several independent containers from collectively overcommitting a laptop VM. A budget-aware scheduler makes the expensive receiver workflow more predictable and gives users enough progress information to distinguish a long compilation from a hang.

7. Make installed demos and task-specific environment checks dependable (fpga-2hx.7, P2, weighted score 4.44/5).
The first successful replay is a compelling entry point, but it should work from a normal installation and should not require model credentials. A task-aware doctor can say exactly what SHA replay, Wi-Fi mapping or optional XLS needs instead of reporting one broad ready flag.

8. Turn failures into typed diagnostics and reproducible development cases (fpga-2hx.8, P2, weighted score 4.36/5).
A syntax error, incorrect output and a VM memory failure call for different actions. Stable failure categories and a minimal replay bundle help both humans and the repair loop work on the actual problem. Preserving the failing stream also avoids rerunning a long suite just to recover overwritten evidence.

9. Give generated receiver stages explicit, checked interface contracts (fpga-2hx.9, P2, weighted score 4.20/5).
Separately verified blocks can still fail when composed with incompatible rates, reset rules or packing. A small shared contract for the existing four stages makes those assumptions reviewable and catches mismatches before a full receiver build. It also reduces dependence on fragile textual substitutions without promising automatic hardware architecture discovery.

10. Broaden adversarial streaming and rejection/recovery coverage (fpga-2hx.10, P2, weighted score 4.20/5).
Passing one stall phase or reset location does not establish behavior at packet boundaries, during output drain or at counter rebasing. Seeded adversarial schedules can uncover boundary failures while preserving the strong tests already present. The missing unsupported-header case is a concrete coverage gap, not a reason to expand the decoder beyond legacy PHY scope.

11. Measure Wi-Fi reception quality against the floating reference (fpga-2hx.11, P2, weighted score 4.12/5).
Exact packet bytes on successful cases cannot quantify how often the hardware loses packets under noise. Paired sensitivity curves show whether bounded arithmetic and survivor history cause a practical regression relative to the existing floating decoder. This directly addresses a documented discrepancy and produces useful guidance for future area reductions.

12. Build a reproducible small-kernel benchmark corpus and trial runner (fpga-2hx.12, P2, weighted score 4.12/5).
A repeatable corpus tells maintainers whether a change improves general translation or only one demo. Starting with bounded FIR and dot-product kernels adds useful signal without building a benchmark bureaucracy. Repeated trials and complete failure accounting make model, prompt and architecture experiments interpretable.

13. Add bounded CI tiers that exercise the full receiver and installed package (fpga-2hx.13, P2, weighted score 4.20/5).
A local success is easier to maintain when regressions in package assets, Wi-Fi compilation and mapped memory behavior become visible automatically. Full receiver runs are expensive, so the right improvement is an explicit tiered test contract with retained evidence and honest skips.

14. Optimize the receiver toward the existing compact resource goal (fpga-2hx.14, P2, weighted score 4.04/5).
Reducing area could make the receiver useful on smaller devices, but guessing at RTL simplifications risks losing the scheduling behavior that now sustains input. A measured, stage-attributed optimization campaign focuses effort where resource savings are real and retains throughput and decoding quality as hard constraints.

15. Import measured Vivado implementation evidence for a named part (fpga-2hx.15, P3, weighted score 3.88/5).
The largest remaining credibility gap for a deployable FPGA core is whether it can meet its clock target after implementation. A portable evidence importer and optional runner connect the current verification artifacts to a licensed external tool environment without making Vivado a dependency for local replay.

NOT SELECTED
Scoped formal proofs for small blocks: Valuable follow-on after explicit ABIs; first resolve frontend, reset assumptions and proof-engine support. Do not make full-receiver proof the laptop acceptance gate.
Automatic fixed-point range and error analysis: Broad analysis requires numerical semantics beyond the current finite contracts; begin with explicit input metadata and measured kernels.
Automatic architecture/decomposition search: The current interfaces are hand-specified; checked composition and baseline campaigns should precede this research expansion.
General IEEE-754 hardware translation: Large semantic and resource expansion beyond the demonstrated bounded fixed-point route.
Board integration and live RF receive demo: Requires a named board, RF front end and constraints not provided in this repository; preserve an optional handoff first.
Browser dashboard for experiment runs: An offline inspect/report flow addresses the immediate evidence problem with less infrastructure.
Distributed remote verification farm: First fix local stage reuse, provenance and admission control; remote orchestration adds trust and deployment work.
Model/provider tournament and automatic model routing: Repeated comparable trials are a prerequisite; routing before evidence risks optimizing anecdotal outcomes.
Cloud result registry with shared accounts: No demonstrated need for a service, tenancy or hosted storage; relocatable local bundles suffice.
General variable-latency streaming contract: Changes the core fixed-cycle interface and scorer model; check existing Wi-Fi stage interfaces first.
AXI-Stream/AXI-Lite integration wrapper library: Useful with a named integration target; avoid selecting bus semantics without a consumer.
New FFT and FEC algorithm portfolio: Sensitivity and hotspot measurements should identify whether alternate algorithms address a real limit.
Power estimation and thermal optimization: Requires implementation and credible activity data before claims become useful.
Automatic execution of uploaded Python/MATLAB oracles: Would expand the execution/trust boundary; retain independently supplied trusted vectors.
Broad code formatting and module rewrite: Readable code is helpful, but concrete evidence, runtime and integration gaps provide stronger user value.

EXECUTION
Start with evidence core fpga-2hx.1.1 and resources core fpga-2hx.4.1. Use br ready --type task --limit 0 --json; parent-child links are organizational, explicit blocks edges carry execution prerequisites. Unit checks branch alongside integration and E2E joins both. All 15 features have four implementation/integration/unit/E2E tasks; no feature closes until its real evidence is linked.

BOUNDARIES
Preserve existing independent oracles, exact full-width numerical comparisons, cycle/reset/order checks, networkless tool isolation, replay, held-out candidate freezing and all current demo functionality. Implementation may add evidence but must not relabel simulation as physical timing or component success as end-to-end success.
Live model campaigns are explicit and bounded. The licensed Vivado runner is an external prerequisite for its real-execution task; parser and handoff development can proceed without it. A measured compact optimization shortfall remains explicit.

DEFINITION OF DONE
This umbrella closes only when all selected features have completed their defined implementation and validation, including required external evidence. Creating or refining the plan is not implementation completion. The markdown report is a convenient view; every feature/task remains independently actionable.

title: Make generation and audit recovery durable and deterministic
description:
Rank 2 of 15; incremental improvement, not an implemented result.

BACKGROUND AND OBSERVED GAP
translate.translate compares source, contract, vector digests and provider/model on resume, but omits image identity, synthesis mode and replay-file identity. It writes history after evaluation and can leave summary.json in_progress on interruption. Wi-Fi backend, Viterbi and receiver loops independently reuse response.json files with fewer identity checks. The shared write_json already uses atomic replacement and should be reused.

USER VALUE AND RATIONALE
A failed container or interrupted laptop session should cost unfinished work, not an entire experiment. Resume must also preserve what was actually tested: changing from RTL-only to mapping or replaying a different proposal cannot inherit an old success. Persisting the selected candidate before opening audit data makes the research boundary inspectable. The benefit is particularly concrete for the Wi-Fi flow, where builds take many minutes and each stage currently has its own recovery behavior.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH
Add an explicit per-run journal with prepared, generation, development, frozen-selection, audit, passed, failed and interrupted states plus per-stage completion. Snapshot immutable inputs and execution policy, enforce exclusive run ownership, recover only complete committed artifacts, and preserve previous results. Share lifecycle helpers across existing loops without forcing their different interfaces into one evaluator. Audit failure remains terminal for candidate selection.

ACCEPTANCE
No stale success survives an identity mismatch or interruption. A saved generation response is reused without pretending prior tool execution applies to a new environment. All generator paths follow the same candidate-freeze and terminal-audit rules.

RISKS AND BOUNDARIES
Avoid silently spending new model calls during recovery; preserve round accounting. Treat stale locks cautiously and retain journals rather than deleting another active run.
Preserve existing independent oracles, exact full-width numerical comparisons, cycle/reset/order checks, networkless tool isolation, replay, held-out candidate freezing and all current demo functionality. Implementation may add evidence but must not relabel simulation as physical timing or component success as end-to-end success.

COMPLETION
All implementation, adoption, unit-test and real-E2E child tasks must be complete with linked evidence. Planning creation does not close this feature.
